title: Write-Back Buffer
statement: Design a write-back buffer that holds one pending write and forwards reads to the updated value when necessary. When a write is pending and a read targets the same address, the buffered value should be returned instead of the older memory value. The buffer should commit data on the next clock cycle.
module_signature: module write_back_buffer(input clk, input rst, input wr_en, input [3:0] addr, input [7:0] data_in, input rd_en, input [3:0] rd_addr, output reg [7:0] data_out, output reg pending);
behavior: pending is 1 when a write is staged but not yet committed.
Reads to the pending address return the buffered data.
rst clears the pending buffer state.
All state updates occur on the rising edge of clk.
rst is active-high and synchronous unless the problem statement explicitly says otherwise.
Use non-blocking assignments in clocked always blocks.
Outputs must never depend on uninitialized x/z state after reset.
When rst is asserted on a rising edge, registered outputs reset to their documented initial values.
constraints: Do not use actual external memory primitives; model the buffer behavior explicitly.
example:
wr_en addr data_in rd_en rd_addr | pending data_out
1 0010 10101010 1 0010 | 1 10101010
hint: Track the pending address and data separately from the memory array.
